title: Steam Distribution Header
model_title: Steam Distribution Header with Branch Take-offs, Drip Leg Trap Station & PRV Station

introduction.definition: A steam distribution header receives steam from the boilers and distributes it to the plant. Branches leave from the top so they take dry steam; the header slopes to drip legs where steam traps remove condensate; a pressure-reducing station supplies lower-pressure users. Insulation, supports and guides handle heat loss and thermal expansion.
applications: Plant steam distribution to process heaters, turbines and tracing
key_points: Drip legs every ≈ 30–50 m and at low points

pressure.title: Dry steam at the right pressure
pressure.description: The header carries boiler-pressure steam. Branches leave from the top so they take dry steam, not the condensate that runs along the bottom. Drip legs of full header bore every ≈ 30–50 m (and at low points / before risers) collect condensate, which a trap removes; without them slugs of water cause water hammer and erosion. A PRV station drops the pressure for users that need lower pressure; latent heat per kg rises as pressure falls, and a downstream safety valve protects the low-pressure side.

foundation: Supports designed for operating, test and wind/seismic loads; allow thermal movement of connected piping.
alignment: Vertical vessels plumb; nozzles and supports loaded within limits.
piping: Relief protection per code, drains at low points, isolations for inspection; slope lines to drains.
commissioning: Pressure test; set and seal relief valves; check instruments and drains; register with the authority where required.

lubrication: No routine lubrication on static parts; lubricate valve stems and actuators per maker.

causes: Failed trap, no drip leg, wrong slope

safety: Hot surfaces; isolate and depressurise before work; never open a hot drain into a closed space.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Steam Distribution Header.
Check pressures and trap discharge.
Trap survey; inspect insulation.
Overhaul PRV and safety valves.
Watch for water hammer: bangs, pipe movement. Common cause: failed trap, no drip leg, wrong slope.
Watch for steam loss through trap: live steam at discharge. Common cause: trap failed open.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
